MESSAGE:
Hiya! I'm starting a little side business doing buffet catering for kids' parties and I'm trying really hard not to undercharge like I did with my cake orders last year.

Can you help me name it? I do mostly party platters and cupcakes. And a cute one-line tagline for my Instagram bio would be amazing. Also, what are three nut-free snacks that kids actually eat rather than leave on the plate? Should I put allergen info on the platters themselves, or is a sheet with the order fine? Just what's best practice for a small caterer, not legal advice.

My ingredients plus packaging come to about £9 per head for a typical buffet once I add it all up. I want a 40% profit margin on every booking. I worked out that means charging £12.60 per head (£9 plus 40%). Is that right? What should I actually charge per head?

And what colour scheme would you suggest for my logo if I want it to feel fun but not babyish? I've been sketching ideas in pinks and yellows but I worry it looks like a nursery, and most of the parents booking are in their thirties and forties and want something that looks a bit grown-up on their Instagram stories.

Thanks so much xx Sorry for all the questions, I'm new to this! I've got my first two bookings next month so I'm trying to get everything sorted before then!

RESPONSE:
Congrats on the bookings! Here's everything in order.

## 1. Business names

- **Little Feast Co.**
- **Party Platter Club**
- **Crumbs & Confetti**
- **The Tiny Table**
- **Sprinkle & Spread**
- **Nibbles & Bows**

My favourite is **Crumbs & Confetti**: it's playful, it suggests both cupcakes and party food, and it doesn't sound babyish. Before you commit, check that the Instagram handle, domain and Companies House name are free.

## 2. Instagram tagline

- *"Party food the kids devour and the parents can actually photograph."*
- *"Platters, cupcakes & zero party-prep stress 🎉"*
- *"Kids' party buffets, done deliciously."*

## 3. Three nut-free snacks kids actually eat

1. **Cheese & ham (or cheese & tomato) pinwheels** made with puff pastry or wraps. They're bite-sized and familiar, and they always disappear.
2. **Mini sausage rolls or cocktail sausages**, which are reliably the first thing gone.
3. **Fruit skewers or cups** with strawberries, melon and **halved** grapes. Halve grapes lengthways for under-5s because whole ones are a choking risk. Bright colours help kids actually pick them up.

**Tip:** check every packaged ingredient for "may contain nuts" warnings, including wraps, pastry, chocolate and sprinkles. Keep your nut-free claims accurate. "Made without nuts" is safer wording than "nut-free" unless your whole kitchen is controlled.

## 4. Allergen info: platters or sheet?

Best practice is **both**:

- **A small label or tent card on each platter** listing the 14 major allergens it contains, e.g. *"Cheese pinwheels: Contains gluten, milk, egg."* At a party, the sheet stays in the kitchen and the food goes to the table, so the label is what people actually see.
- **A full allergen sheet with the order** for the parent who booked, so they can check before the day.

Also ask about allergies **at booking** on your order form, and keep a record. If you sell anything pre-packed, look up Natasha's Law and your local council's food safety guidance. You'll also need to register as a food business with your council at least 28 days before trading, so do that now if you haven't already.

## 5. Pricing: is £12.60 right?

**Not quite.** This is the most common pricing mix-up, so it's good you checked.

- **£9 + 40% = £12.60** is a 40% **markup**, which gives you a margin of only **28.6%** (£3.60 ÷ £12.60).
- A 40% **margin** means profit is 40% of the *price*. The formula is **cost ÷ (1 − margin)**:

> **£9 ÷ 0.60 = £15.00 per head**
> Check: £15 − £9 = £6 profit, and £6 ÷ £15 = 40% ✅

So **£15 per head** is the minimum for a 40% margin on ingredients and packaging.

That still doesn't cover your **time**, though, and undercharging for time is probably what happened with the cakes. Your £9 should also include a share of:
- Your hours for shopping, prep, cooking, assembly, delivery and washing up
- Fuel and delivery
- Platters or disposables you don't get back
- Utilities, insurance and food hygiene certification
- Card or payment fees

For example, if a 20-head party takes you 6 hours and you value your time at £15/hour, that's £90, or £4.50 per head. Your true cost becomes £13.50, and a 40% margin gives **£22.50 per head**.

**My suggestions:**
- Charge **at least £15/head**, and realistically **£18–£22** once labour is included. Compare with local competitors, since kids' party catering in the UK often sits around £8–£20/head depending on area and what's included.
- Set a **minimum order** (e.g. 15 heads, or a £200 minimum) so small bookings are still worth your time.
- Add a **delivery fee** based on distance.
- Price cupcakes separately as an add-on (e.g. £2.50–£3.50 each), which raises the order value.

## 6. Logo colour scheme: fun but grown-up

You don't have to drop pink and yellow. Soften them and add a strong grounding colour:

**Option A: Grown-up pastels**
- Dusty rose `#D8A7A0`
- Butter yellow `#F3D98B`
- Deep navy or charcoal `#2B2D42` (for text and logo)
- Cream background `#FAF5EE`

**Option B: Warm & modern**
- Terracotta/coral `#E07A5F`
- Mustard `#E9B44C`
- Sage green `#9DB5A0`
- Off-white `#F7F3EC`

**Option C: Bold & playful**
- Tomato red `#E63946`
- Sunshine yellow `#FFC93C`
- Black or espresso `#1E1E1E`
- White

What makes it look grown-up rather than nursery:
- **One dark anchor colour** (navy, charcoal or black) for text
- **Muted, slightly dusty tones** rather than bright candy shades
- **Clean or bold typography.** Avoid bubbly "baby" fonts and try a chunky serif or a rounded sans instead.
- **Plenty of cream or white space**, so it looks good in Instagram stories

I'd go with **Option A**. It keeps the pink and yellow you already like but will look polished on parents' stories.

## Quick pre-launch checklist
- ☐ Register with your local council (28 days before trading)
- ☐ Level 2 Food Hygiene certificate
- ☐ Public liability insurance
- ☐ Order form with allergy questions
- ☐ Allergen labels and sheets
- ☐ Deposit policy (e.g. 30–50% non-refundable to secure the date)

Good luck with the first two bookings, you've got this! 🎉
